title: Borodin-Kostochka Conjecture
statement_text: For every graph $G$ such that $\Delta(G)\geq 9$, if $\omega(G)\leq\Delta(G)-1$, then $\chi(G)\leq\Delta(G)-1$.
context_text: Borodin and Kostochka conjectured in 1977 that graphs with maximum degree at least 9 and clique number at most $\Delta(G)-1$ can be properly colored with at most $\Delta(G)-1$ colors. The assumption $\Delta(G)\geq 9$ is necessary, as shown by the graph $C_5\boxtimes K_3$.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for the stronger correspondence chromatic number $\chi_{DP}$, showing that for every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\geq 3\cdot 10^9$, $\chi_{DP}(G)\leq\max(\omega(G),\Delta(G)-1)$.
paper_title: On Borodin-Kostochka conjecture for correspondence coloring

title: Question 5
statement_text: What is the smallest number $\Delta_{0}$ such that every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\geq\Delta_{0}$ and $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)-1$ satisfies $\chi(G)=\chi_{\ell}(G)=\chi_{DP}(G)$?
context_text: $\chi_\ell(G)$ is the list chromatic number (the least $k$ such that $G$ can be properly coloured from any lists of size $k$). $\chi_{DP}(G)$ is the correspondence (DP) chromatic number: a $k$-correspondence assignment gives each vertex $v$ a list $L(v)$ of at least $k$ colours and each edge $uv$ a (not necessarily perfect) matching $\Pi(uv)$ between $\{u\}\times L(u)$ and $\{v\}\times L(v)$; an $(L,\Pi)$-colouring picks $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v$ such that $\{(u,\varphi(u)),(v,\varphi(v))\}\notin\Pi(uv)$ for every edge; and $\chi_{DP}(G)$ is the least $k$ such that every $k$-correspondence assignment admits such a colouring. Always $\chi(G)\le\chi_\ell(G)\le\chi_{DP}(G)\le\Delta(G)+1$. The Borodin–Kostochka conjecture asserts that $\Delta(G)\ge9$ and $\omega(G)\le\Delta(G)-1$ imply $\chi(G)\le\Delta(G)-1$; Reed proved this for $\Delta(G)\ge10^{14}$, and Choi, Kierstead and Rabern proved the list version for $\Delta(G)\ge10^{20}$. The authors prove the correspondence version: for $\Delta\ge3\cdot10^9$, every graph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and clique number at most $\Delta-1$ has $\chi_{DP}(G)\le\Delta-1$, so that graphs with $\Delta(G)\ge 3\cdot10^9$ and $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)-1$ satisfy $\chi=\chi_\ell=\chi_{DP}=\Delta(G)-1$; this gives $\Delta_0\le3\cdot10^9$. The three parameters trivially coincide when $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)+1$, and also when $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)\ge3$ by the correspondence analogue of Brooks' theorem.
paper_title: On Borodin-Kostochka conjecture for correspondence coloring
